deeper.title: What the price assumes
deeper.text: The price assumes about 39% a year growth in free cash flow for 10 years, then 3% (discount rate 9.9% = 10-year Treasury 4.9% + 5%; base: sales × its 3-year median free-cash margin (3%), because current free cash flow is negative). For comparison, sales grew 31% last year; 18%/yr over 3 years — the market expects faster growth than the company has recently delivered.

deeper.title: Return on capital
deeper.text: Not meaningful (the company holds more cash than its debt plus equity, or data is missing); return on shareholders' equity 8% (3 years ago -6%).

deeper.title: Signed future revenue
deeper.text: Customer prepayments not yet earned (deferred revenue): $333M, up from $64M a year ago.

deeper.title: Earnings-quality red flags
flags: Inventory up 105% vs quarterly sales up 50% (days of inventory 148 → 211). Products may be building up unsold — a warning sign in chip cycles.
Profit leans on non-operating gains: net income $945M vs operating income $96M over the last 12 months (e.g. investment gains or one-offs that may not repeat).

deeper.title: Multi-year view
deeper.text: Sales grew 18%/yr over 3 years and 20%/yr over 5 years; operating margin today 2% vs a 3-year range of -3–12% (median 5%): in the middle of its range.

deeper.title: Cash returned to shareholders
deeper.text: No buybacks or dividends reported over the last 12 months. Share count up 5.9% from a year ago (stock pay outpacing buybacks — dilution).

deeper.title: Analyst estimates
deeper.text: Next year's earnings-per-share estimate $15.67, up 19% in 90 days (up 12% in the last 30); 2 analysts raised, 1 cut in 30 days. This year's earnings-per-share estimate $10.38, up 24% in 90 days (up 10% in the last 30); 1 analyst raised, 1 cut in 30 days. Source: Yahoo (unofficial).

deeper.title: Where sales come from
deeper.text: By segment, latest quarter vs a year earlier: Datacenter & Communications 82% of sales, up 79%; Industrial 18% of sales, down 15%. Source: 10-Q XBRL.

tiles.title: Earnings per share
tiles.sub: +80% vs a year ago · $4.68 over 12 months (GAAP)
tiles.read: Profit per share grew 80% vs sales 50% (latest quarter vs a year earlier): profits are outgrowing sales, so margins are widening.
tiles.explain: EPS = profit divided by the number of shares. The quarterly figures are the 'adjusted' EPS analysts track (Yahoo); the 12-month figure is the official GAAP number from SEC filings.

tiles.title: Earnings vs forecasts
tiles.sub: last 8 reports · bars = EPS beat (+) or miss (−) vs the average forecast
tiles.read: Beat forecasts 8 quarters running, but the beats are shrinking (17% → 5%): the bar is getting harder to clear.
tiles.explain: A 'beat' means reported EPS came in above the average analyst forecast. Source: Yahoo (unofficial).

tiles.title: Sales growth
tiles.sub: latest quarter +50% vs a year earlier · 12-month sales $7.9B
tiles.read: Latest quarter: sales up 50% vs a year earlier and speeding up (from 21% two quarters ago): demand is strengthening.
tiles.explain: Headline: sales over the last 12 months vs the 12 months before. Bars: each quarter's sales vs the same quarter a year earlier.

tiles.title: Profit margins
tiles.read: Each $100 of sales leaves $1 of operating profit, about the same as a year ago.
tiles.explain: Operating margin = operating profit ÷ sales. Gross margin = what's left after the direct cost of the product.

tiles.title: Free cash flow
tiles.read: Free cash flow is negative: it's spending more (often on new capacity) than the business brings in.
tiles.explain: Free cash flow = cash from operations minus spending on equipment and buildings: money the company could return or reinvest.

tiles.title: Price vs profits (P/E)
tiles.read: You pay 47× last year's profit (lower than 62% of the last 5 years); only 14× next year's forecast, so the market expects profits to jump.
tiles.explain: P/E = share price ÷ earnings per share. Forward P/E uses next year's forecast earnings.

tiles.title: Next earnings
tiles.read: Reports Feb 3; analysts expect EPS of $2.40, up 86% from a year ago. It usually moves about 10% the day after, so expect a swing.
tiles.explain: Consensus = the average analyst forecast (Yahoo, unofficial). The typical move is the average size of the stock's next-day move after its last reports, not an options-implied figure.

tiles.title: Company outlook

tiles.explain: Guidance = what management says it expects for the next quarter or year, from its 8-K earnings release.
